account:
Today is day 1, just after nine. I am at town hall during office hours, due at the mill at ten for a grain inspection. Later I have lunch at home, council letters at one, tea with the neighbour at the east-bank cottage at three, and office business at four-thirty.

The unresolved unusual business is a vague rumor about a bridge or port change. I have not established that any such change is planned. Yesterday the secretary traced a named link to Townsfolk 03, who directed her to the innkeeper; the innkeeper denied proposing or announcing a change. The builder reported no confirmed bridge defects, and relayed Freight's report of undamaged roads and an uneventful ferry crossing. Those are reports, not my own inspection findings.

I want to speak directly with Townsfolk 03 to learn what they actually heard or saw. The secretary has not confirmed a meeting. The neighbour offered to relay my invitation but says they have not encountered Townsfolk 03, and has asked the secretary where to find them. The neighbour expects our usual tea today. I have no evidence that either the neighbour or Townsfolk 03 is arranging anything secretly.

This morning the builder requested a paid maintenance survey. I authorized a visual inspection of the bridge deck, rails and accessible supports, and ferry-landing planks and lighting: two emeralds payable upon written findings, with no repairs or alterations authorized. The builder explicitly said there was no confirmed damage. This appears to be a condition survey, not evidence that the rumored changes are happening. I supplied one additional emerald for a writable report book; the builder has now left to buy it and inspect. The secretary retains my original appointment book, reports no new correspondence, and has requested funds for writing supplies. Her request included a report book already funded through the builder, so only her separate record book still appears unfunded. For now, the rumor remains unverified; I need a firsthand account rather than treating repeated talk as proof.
